questions.prompt: What's the difference between Git and GitHub?
options: Git records history on your computer; GitHub is a website that stores repositories online
GitHub is a newer version of Git
Git is for Python and GitHub is for everything else
questions.explanation: Git is the tool. GitHub is one popular place to keep and share Git repositories.

questions.prompt: Why make a branch instead of editing `main` directly?
options: So you can work safely without changing the official version until your change is reviewed
questions.explanation: Branches are safe drafts. `main` only changes when a reviewed pull request is merged.

questions.prompt: Match each command or idea to its meaning.
pairs: Send your commits up to GitHub
Bring others' commits down to you
Ask for your branch to be reviewed and merged
Nickname for your repository on GitHub
questions.explanation: Push up, pull down, PR for review.

questions.prompt: Create and switch to a new branch called `fix-fees`: `git switch __ fix-fees`
questions.explanation: `-c` means *create*. Older guides use `git checkout -b fix-fees`, which does the same thing.
